Collapse an identity graph into a master identity table

generate_master_identity_table.Rd

Finds the connected components of an entity type's identity graph (built up via repeated add_to_identity_graph() calls) and collapses each component into a single master identity, assigned an ID like "PERSON-1", "PERSON-2", .... The resulting table has one row per master identity and one list-column per distinct id_type seen (e.g. email, unikey), each holding every identifier value that resolved to that identity.

Usage

generate_master_identity_table(
  env_name = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE,
  id_prefix = NULL,
  store_in_env = TRUE
)

Arguments

env_name

Optional entity type name (e.g. "person"). If NULL (the default), a master table is generated for every entity type currently initialised via init_id_envs(), returned as a named list.

verbose

If TRUE (the default), print progress messages.

id_prefix

Prefix used for generated master IDs. Defaults to the upper-cased env_name followed by "-" (e.g. "PERSON-").

store_in_env

If TRUE (the default), also store the resulting table so get_master_table() can retrieve it later without regenerating it.

Value

A tibble with one row per master identity: an ID column named "<env_name>_id", and one list-column per id_type found in the graph. If env_name is NULL, a named list of such tibbles, one per entity type.
